thread:
alex-cs: FYI from ACME — their app suddenly saw latency spikes and auth failures. They say requests are landing in us-west instead of eu-central; getting 200ms+ extra and intermittent 401s. Example header they pasted: `x-region: us-west-2`, `x-request-id: r12345`. Can someone triage?
maya-support: do we have a raw request + timestamp or request-id? need a repro to correlate logs.
acme-dev: here's the sanitized curl we ran: `curl -i -H \"Authorization: Bearer sk-ACME\" -H \"x-request-id: r12345\" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate` -> response 401 + header `x-region: us-west-2`. Happened 2026-01-15T11:02Z. Also saw a billing/egress jump on our invoice.
jonas-infra: looking up r12345... ingress shows the request was routed to a us-west pool because the failover policy for `/v1/generate` had priorities serialized oddly. The saved policy payload looks like it reordered priorities. Pulling the config now.
jonas-infra: ```json
{
  \"route\": \"/v1/generate\",
  \"failover\": {
    \"priority\": [2,1,3],
    \"weights\": {\"eu-central\": 0.7, \"us-west\": 0.3},
    \"sticky_ttl_sec\": 3600
  }
}
```
leila-sre: if the UI/string serialization flips the array the backend treats the first element as highest priority, that would send sessions to us-west. Sticky TTL plus an existing cookie could keep subsequent calls pinned there — explains cross-region hits and auth scope mismatches if tokens were region-scoped.
maya-support: customer says the issue started right after they edited a route in the console. Any recent console changes?
deploy-bot: deploy log: \"Commit 2519876400: route update /v1/generate — priority serialized as '1,2,3'\"
jonas-infra: I see a console save by maya-support at 2519876400. It appears the client side serialized the priority array as a CSV string; backend split it and then our parser applied reverse order when converting to internal enum. Edge-case bug.
jonas-infra: repro steps I used: 1) create a failover policy in UI with priorities [eu-central, us-west] 2) save -> UI sends `priority: \"eu-central,us-west\"` 3) backend splits and pushes into internal vector but a previous sort() call ends up reversing in some cases. Repro is consistent on my local.
leila-sre: mitigation plan: (a) hotfix parser to preserve order (b) invalidate sticky cookies for the route so sessions re-evaluate region routing (c) add request header `x-preferred-region` support as opt-in pinning so customers can override until fix.
maya-support: I've told ACME to clear client cookies and rotate their key as a stopgap; also offered the `x-preferred-region: eu-central` header. They applied it and reported better latency.
alex-cs: they also want an explanation and any credits for the unexpected egress charges. Please capture billing delta.
jonas-infra: created incident INC-2026-0031. Action items: [1] patch parser and deploy to canary (ETA 2h), [2] invalidate sticky cookies for `/v1/generate` across edge (ETA 30m), [3] add telemetry to detect priority/weight mismatches (follow-up), [4] run egress delta calc for ACME and coordinate credits with finance.
leila-sre: hotfix merged to canary, running integration. If canary looks good we'll roll to prod in waves. Monitoring latencies and cross-region metrics now.
acme-dev: thanks @maya-support @jonas-infra @leila-sre — confirmed our traffic went back to eu-central after the cookie purge and the patch on canary. We'll monitor overnight.
maya-support: closing loop for now — keeping the incident open until prod rollout completes. :white_check_mark:
